title: Every Order ID, Once
description:
`source_orders` is the live production system; `warehouse_orders` is what landed in the analytics warehouse after the last sync. They're supposed to agree, but don't always.

Report every distinct `order_id` that appears in **either** system, with no duplicates even if an id appears in both.

Name the column `order_id`. Return the result in any order.
hint: Plain UNION already removes duplicates across the two SELECTs — you don't need DISTINCT on top of it.
outputExplanation: source_orders has ids 1, 2, 3, 4 and warehouse_orders has ids 1, 2, 5. Combined without duplicates, the result is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

tests.name: Example
All three systems fully agree
Completely disjoint across all three
Source has an accidental duplicate row
Only source has any data
tests.seedSql: INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'Ann Lee',120.0),(2,'Ben Kim',80.0),(3,'Cy Ortiz',45.5);

tests.name: Same order, inconsistent name formatting
Matching ids, mismatched amounts
Single matching order everywhere

tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0),(2,'B',200.0);

tests.name: Completely disjoint sets
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO source_orders VALUES (1,'A',10.0),(2,'B',20.0);
INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (3,'C',30.0),(4,'D',40.0);

tests.name: Duplicates within source
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO warehouse_orders VALUES (1,'A',100.0);
